advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the docstring: only 3 of the ~19 diffing-suite `_load_module` copies use the cache-first/__file__-guarded form; they are not 'three byte-identical copies'.
evidence: Comment at line 39-40: 'The three diffing suites carry byte-identical copies of the helper; test_differ.py is the canonical one.'
search_files `def _load_module` under tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing returns ~19 distinct files (test_differ.py, test_inbound_differ.py, test_outbound_differ.py, test_link_dedup.py, ...).
search_files `cached = sys.modules.get(name)` returns only 3 hits: test_differ.py:47, test_differ_conflict_resolution.py:44, test_differ_quarantine_suppression.py:49.
test_inbound_differ.py:29-35 shows the simple form: `sys.modules[name] = mod` with no cache-first lookup and no `__file__` guard, which is NOT byte-identical to test_differ.py:47-55.
advisory.finding: The module docstring / inline comment states 'The three diffing suites carry byte-identical copies of the helper; test_differ.py is the canonical one,' but this is factually wrong: ~19 diffing-suite files define `_load_module`, and only 3 carry the cache-first, __file__-guarded form — the rest use the simple `sys.modules[name] = mod` variant, so the copies are neither three nor byte-identical.
scenarios: A maintainer reads the docstring and believes all diffing helpers are identical and jointly pinned.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either parametrize the test over all diffing `_load_module` copies or narrow the docstring's claim to state coverage is limited to test_differ.py.
evidence: Line 37: `_DIFFER_TEST = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "test_differ.py"` — the test reads only test_differ.py.
Module docstring: 'a restated copy would keep passing while the original rotted' — the anti-rot argument is asserted for the suites in general, but only test_differ.py is actually exercised.
test_inbound_differ.py:29-35 uses the unguarded helper form and is not referenced by this test, so a regression there is invisible to it.
advisory.finding: The test pins the invariants only against `test_differ.py`'s helper, but ~15 other diffing suites carry their own (unguarded) `_load_module`; dropping the __file__ guard or restoring setdefault in any of those copies would NOT turn this test red, undercutting the docstring's 'tracks the shipped code so a copy cannot rot' guarantee for all but one file.
scenarios: A future edit drops the __file__ guard from test_outbound_differ.py or test_inbound_differ.py; suites go green and this identity test stays green.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix or remove the docstring reference to the non-existent `test_user_guide_commands.py`.
evidence: Line 28: 'the same reasoning `test_user_guide_commands.py` uses for parsing the guide at runtime.'
search_files `test_user_guide_commands` returns only two mentions (this file and a comment in tests/unit/test_user_guide_dc_docs.py:14) — no file named test_user_guide_commands.py exists.
advisory.finding: The docstring cites `test_user_guide_commands.py` as an existing precedent for the load-by-path pattern, but no such file exists in the repository.
scenarios: A reader tries to find the cited precedent to understand the pattern and cannot.
